title: Projection review: before and after
description: Compare the same episode, camera and playback time. The Flexiv center candidate preserves its corrected rotation. DexWild now uses all 30 fps with smoother overlay edges and unchanged poses. Dexora’s prior overlay is rejected; all four raw views and the investigation are available. These display changes do not modify canonical or training datasets. ALOHA remains excluded.

cases.title: Flexiv · align the ceramic bowls
cases.finding: The remaining center offset comes from a visually tuned camera prior: an older fit deliberately shifted another clip’s TCP target 40 pixels right. The session repair changed only rotation and retained that translation. At 10 seconds, the displayed origin is about 44 px right and 28 px above the visible fin midpoint.
cases.change: This candidate changes translation only. The corrected quaternion, widths and lens stay exactly the same. The before video is the orientation-restored projection; the after video centers the same primitive more closely on independent frames. This is a display candidate, not a measured physical TCP calibration.
remaining: Measure camera intrinsics and the physical relationship between the source TCP and tactile-fin contact points; image alignment alone cannot distinguish camera translation, principal point and local origin offsets.
Replace the simple boxes with measured fin/linkage geometry: the visible midpoint still shifts about 23 px as the fingers open.
Validate fast opening/closing timing and additional episodes from the same session before generalizing.

remaining: Repair both per-frame end-effector poses and per-episode anchors in a new versioned export; the gallery correction does not repair training data.
Resolve source sampling holds, which reach 0.5–0.7 s in displayed cameras and 1.6 s in one other view. A single time shift is not justified.
Measure contact-point projection error and validate the nominal wrist-camera calibration.

cases.title: ManipForce · battery insertion
cases.finding: The previous gallery showed raw video because the export lacked usable camera-to-tool translation, a gripper-width channel and CAD. The supplied state already represents TCP.
cases.change: Added the supplied CAD and an episode-specific optical-camera fit using the visible marker perimeter and CAD recess. The overlay preserves the world TCP and uses a fixed 12.571 mm opening inferred from this clip. The marker-to-TCP offset is not applied to the state again. The second D405 video is restored in the camera selector as a raw reference; it has no validated overlay.
remaining: Confirm the physical marker dimensions: the fit assumes the white perimeter occupies the 12 mm CAD recess, while the upstream black-marker assumption is 21 mm. Image fit alone cannot establish metric scale.
Validate device intrinsics and the inferred opening, and calibrate the second D405 view before projecting into it.
Create and validate a separate training export if the fitted optical-camera motion is adopted; it differs from the legacy trajectory.

cases.title: Dexora · articulation
cases.finding: The camera-frame overlay is rejected: both the external-camera geometry and wrist optical mounts are uncalibrated priors. The projection matrix and video orientation are correct, so changing plotting signs cannot fix the alignment. This episode has four views: external, head, left wrist and right wrist.
cases.change: The review now shows all four raw camera views and no claimed corrected overlay. Fitting visible palm landmarks improves image alignment, but cannot identify optical centers or axis directions: changing the assumed palm landmark by 20 mm moves the fitted external camera by 80.7 mm with similar image errors. The rejected overlay remains linked below for inspection.
remaining: Measure the external-camera intrinsics/distortion and pose relative to the robot, plus each wrist flange-to-optical transform. Palm or flange origins cannot substitute for optical centers.
Correct and calibrate the head optical/body-frame convention. Validate state/video timing independently; the diagnostic fit’s proposed −3-frame shift is not an established correction.
Validate the real hand-joint/model correspondence before using articulated fingertip geometry for calibration.

cases.title: DexWild · camera frames and playback flicker
cases.finding: Two separate issues are present. The old preview skipped two of every three frames and rounded overlay coordinates. The remaining flashes are six horizontally torn exterior-camera frames already present in the original HDF5 recording: 1.97, 2.20, 2.90, 3.43, 3.50 and 7.97 s. They were not introduced by the overlay or MP4 conversion.
cases.change: Restored all 267 source frames at 30 fps, added subpixel overlay edges and made the tracker-loss note persistent. Camera poses and timing remain unchanged. The normal gallery now opens this reviewed exterior overlay, with original raw views selectable. The video retains the six source tears; the capture audit provides a verified frame mask for data filtering.
remaining: For training, use the verified source-frame mask to reject windows overlapping the torn frames. The existing load-time detector catches all six at full rate but misses one at stride 2; its neighboring-frame test is not a complete replacement for source-frame labels.
Validate the tracker-to-thumb-camera optical mount and per-rig fisheye intrinsics. Source pose interpolation at 2.20 s and tracker noise remain separate from the image tears.

cases.title: DROID · AUTOLab failure
cases.finding: The source camera-to-flange translation plus assumed CAD mounting transform leaves a repeatable displacement in both wrist eyes. The former linear jaw mapping also drew a 10.07 mm gap for a recorded zero opening.
cases.change: The width now drives the actual URDF linkage. A single translation fitted jointly to both eyes moves the wrist camera while preserving the world flange, recorded rotation, intrinsics and 63 mm baseline. Only the exact audited episode and input hashes select this fit.
remaining: Camera translation, physical mounting offset and residual CAD error cannot be separated by this fit.
Visible linkage edges still differ; these are not a pixel-perfect or metric-calibration pass.
Other episodes and the low-resolution single-eye samples retain their source camera calibration.
